concepts.definition: Adding a brand-new sprite to the stage from inside an event while the game is running.
concepts.example: Every time you press the A button, a new laser sprite is created.
concepts.pitfall: Creating the sprite once inside when game starts and using the same one for every press: there is only ever one bullet.

concepts.definition: The label the collision rule recognises; if the laser is created with the Bullet kind, the rule finds it.
concepts.example: The rule "when a Bullet hits an Enemy, raise the score" finds the laser of the Bullet kind.
concepts.pitfall: Leaving the kind as Object: the collision event never runs.

concepts.definition: In a collision event, the sprite of the kind written first is this sprite and the second is other sprite.
concepts.example: In the event when a Bullet hits an Enemy, this sprite is the laser and other sprite is the alien.
concepts.pitfall: Mixing the two up and trying to blow up the laser and delete the alien.

concepts.term: Delete when it leaves the world
concepts.definition: A setting that deletes a sprite by itself when it goes off the screen.
concepts.example: A laser that leaves the top of the screen is deleted and the stage does not fill up.
concepts.pitfall: Not turning this setting on: missed bullets pile up and the stage fills up.

concepts.definition: An event that runs once at the moment the button is pressed; holding it down does not start a new run.
concepts.example: If you press A twice, two lasers come out.
concepts.pitfall: Expecting rapid fire from holding the button down.

quiz.prompt: The laser appears at y = 88 and goes up at 140 pixels a second. In how many seconds does the laser's centre reach y = 18?
quiz.explanation: The distance to travel is 88 - 18 = 70 pixels. Time = distance / speed = 70 / 140 = 0.5 seconds. Note: in the real game the sprites have a size, so the collision happens a little before the centres meet.

quiz.prompt:
The laser is created with the "delete when it leaves the world" setting. The collision event is:

```
when a Bullet sprite hits a Enemy sprite:
  change score by 10
  make other sprite explode
```

What happens after the laser hits the alien?
options: The laser is deleted at once too
The laser stops and stays where the alien was
The laser carries on its way and is deleted when it leaves the top of the screen
quiz.explanation: There is no block in the event that deletes the laser; only the alien explodes. The laser keeps going up and is deleted thanks to the setting when it leaves the screen. This bug leads to unneeded bullets piling up on the screen.

quiz.prompt:
The lasers come out and touch the alien, but the score never goes up. Which is the bug?

```
when A button is pressed:
  lazer = new [Laser] sprite, kind [Object]
  set lazer speed x 0, y -140

when a Bullet sprite hits a Enemy sprite:
  change score by 10
```
options: The laser is created with the Object kind; the collision rule expects the Bullet kind
The score should change by 1, not 10
The A button event cannot be used together with a collision
quiz.explanation: The collision rule looks at the sprite's kind. Because the laser is of the Object kind, the Bullet rule never sees it and the score does not change. Creating the laser with the Bullet kind fixes the problem. The speed and score numbers are not wrong.

quiz.prompt: Inside the "when a Bullet sprite hits a Enemy sprite" event, who is "this sprite"?
options: The sprite of the Enemy kind
The sprite of the Bullet kind
quiz.explanation: This sprite is the kind written first in the rule: Bullet. Other sprite is the second kind: Enemy. You use this sprite to delete the laser and other sprite to blow up the alien.

quiz.prompt: The player presses A 5 times a second. Each laser stays on the screen for exactly 2 seconds (then it is deleted). At most, how many lasers are on the screen at the same time?
quiz.explanation: 5 new lasers are created every second and each one lives for 2 seconds: 5 x 2 = 10 lasers are on the screen at the same time. Holding the button down does not raise this number, because it does not count as a new press.
